conviction_note: The baseline's 8-filing history is unusable, so I rebuilt a real one from Yahoo daily closes around the four actual results releases (2025-09-08 +2.39%, 2025-12-11 +0.26%, 2026-03-13 -3.60%, 2026-05-29 -2.08%; median absolute 2.2%, mean -0.76%); against that scale I take a modest negative because the 8 September release is the first company document that must restate the Yamal sanctions paragraph after the stock re-rated +16% in two sessions (22-23 July) on a Greek carve-out whose named beneficiaries are the sponsor's private Arc7 fleet rather than the MLP's two ice-class-1A ships, discounted for the fact that ~6% of that rally has already been given back since 6 August and that 50k shares/day cannot move far on a wording change.

findings.finding: The EU 21st-package carve-out that drove DLNG from $3.32 (16 July) to $3.85 (23 July) is a third-country-deliveries-only derogation expiring 25 July 2027, renewable one year at a time by Council vote and capped at the operator's 2025 volumes; the AIS work identifying the Dynagas vessels it protects names Clean Planet, Clean Vision, Clean Ocean and Clean Horizon - none of which are among the listed partnership's six ships - while DLNG's own Yamal-chartered Lena River last called at Huelva, Spain, an EU import terminal, departing 25 August 2026, i.e. exactly the EU-delivery employment the derogation does not cover.
findings.why_not_priced: Dynagas holds no earnings call and has said nothing in writing since 29 May 2026, when its 6-K still stated that losing the Yamal charters 'would have a material adverse effect' and that it was studying 'the feasibility of lawfully removing the E.U. nexus'; the 8 September release is the first company text after the derogation. If the market had read the derogation's terms rather than the headline it would not have paid +9.17% and +4.34% on 22-23 July and then held most of it - and a $135m MLP with no analyst coverage, no EPS estimate and 41 contracts of total option open interest has no mechanism through which anyone reconciled the Official Journal text with which four hulls actually sit inside the listed entity. Coverage, if this were priced, would look like a note distinguishing the sponsor's Arc7 fleet from the MLP's 1A fleet; no such note exists.
findings.independence: Two separate documents reach the same reading of the text independently of the urgewald analysis: euobserver, 27 July 2026, states the exemption covers LNG 'to third countries' and explicitly not European deliveries (https://euobserver.com/230246/brussels-found-russias-lng-weak-spot-then-carved-out-an-exception-for-a-greek-billionaire/), and High North News, 4 August 2026, gives the 25 July 2027 expiry, the annual Council renewal and the 2025 volume cap (https://en.highnorthnews.com/politics/eu-softens-russian-lng-sanctions-allowing-shipping-and-trading-to-continue-beyond-2027/1115356). The fleet-identity leg is independently checkable against the partnership's own Q1 6-K, which lists its six vessels as Clean Energy, Ob River, Amur River, Arctic Aurora, Yenisei River and Lena River (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm). NOTE ON CLUSTERING: the vessel-identity leg and the destination-split leg both come out of the same urgewald document, so treat them as one source, not two.
findings.source_cluster_note: urgewald 2026-08-18 is one document supporting two legs of this finding; the terms of the derogation are independently sourced to euobserver and High North News.

findings.finding: Clean Energy, the vessel DLNG moved onto a Rio Grande LNG charter 'at higher daily rates' at the end of April 2026, has sat at anchor in Southeast Asia in ballast (draught 8.9 m, speed 0.1 knots) with no destination and no ETA since departing Singapore Anchorage on 5 August 2026 - 33 days idle - while Arctic Aurora, still trading normally (loaded at Melkoya, Norway on 7 September for Klaipeda), is contracted to begin a second seven-year Rio Grande charter between September and November 2026, which would put a third of the six-ship fleet on hire to a project company whose Brownsville trains are not yet producing.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates AIS for a 50k-ADV MLP. This does not touch Q2 revenue - Q2 ended 30 June and time-charter hire is paid whether the ship moves or not - so the channel is the presentation's fleet-employment page and any disclosure of sublet or restructured arrangements with Rio Grande LNG, LLC, plus the Arctic Aurora delivery window. Had the market focused on it, a name whose entire equity story is charter counterparty quality would carry commentary on a pre-operational charterer holding two of six hulls; there is none, and the July rally treated the charter book as de-risked rather than concentrated. I am deliberately sizing this small because the contractual cash flow is unaffected.
findings.independence: Two other vessels checked the same day on separate pages show the idling is not fleet-wide, which is what makes the Clean Energy datum interpretable rather than a data artefact: Ob River is en route Anjeong, Korea (departed 5 September) to Zhuhai, China (https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9315692), and Arctic Aurora departed Melkoya, Norway on 7 September at 18.3 knots for Klaipeda (https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9645970). Separately, the partnership's Q1 6-K is the source for the end-April Rio Grande delivery and the 'higher daily rates' characterisation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm).

findings.finding: Six directors of Dynagas LNG Partners filed initial Section 16 ownership statements on 18 and 30 March 2026, every one of them carrying event date 18 March 2026 - George Prokopiou reporting 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd (50.4% beneficial interest), Alexios Rodopoulos 500 units direct, Dimitrios Anagnostopoulos 'no securities owned' - even though the partnership is exempt from Section 16 as a foreign private issuer under Rule 3a12-3(b), filed a 20-F for FY2025 on 8 April 2026 and has continued filing 6-Ks rather than 10-Qs through 13 August 2026; no Form 4 has followed in the five and a half months since.
findings.why_not_priced: I am filing this at zero because I could not resolve it, not because it is unimportant: it is a genuine contradiction in the filing record that I can document and cannot explain. A board that becomes Section 16 reporting normally means the issuer has concluded it no longer qualifies as a foreign private issuer, which would force 10-Q/10-K/8-K, US-GAAP-only reporting and proxy statements - or it is the compliance footprint of a transaction. Neither has surfaced. If the market had noticed, a $135m MLP would show speculation about domestic-filer conversion or a going-private, and the 8 September event would not be scheduled as a 6-K with no conference call. I refuse to guess a sign, so it carries no directional weight; the band is width, not a view.
findings.independence: none - the only corroboration is that the same EDGAR submissions index shows both the Form 3 cluster and the continuing 6-K/20-F pattern, which is the same source (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001578453.json), and no press, filing or company statement anywhere explains the 18 March 2026 event date.

searched_and_found_nothing: Charter expiry cliff - the door the sweep pointed at - is closed: Yenisei River to Yamal Trade 2033, Lena River 2034, Clean Energy to Rio Grande from April 2026, Arctic Aurora to Rio Grande for ~7 years from Sept-Nov 2026, Ob River and Amur River to SEFE to 2028. Nothing rolls off in 2026-27 that is not already contracted forward, and coverage is 100%/100%/65% for 2026/27/28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm).

Distribution catalyst - there is none. The Q2 common distribution of $0.050 was already declared on 13 August 2026 and the Series A preferred distribution of $0.5625 (44th consecutive) on 23 July 2026, so the 8 September release carries no capital-return news (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/13/3344926/0/en/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-announces-cash-distribution-for-the-quarter-ended-june-30-2026-of-0-050-per-common-unit.html).

Late-report signal - none. DLNG has always reported Q2 in early September; Q2 2025 was released before the open on 8 September 2025, so 8 September 2026 is exactly on cadence, not a delay (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/03/3144042/0/en/Dynagas-LNG-Partners-LP-Announces-Date-for-the-Release-of-the-Second-Quarter-and-Six-Month-2025-Results.html).

The Fayard drydock story - the six Arc7 hulls named as booked into Denmark's Fayard yard in summer 2026 before the January 2027 EU maritime-services ban are Rudolf Samoylovich, Georgiy Brusilov, Boris Davydov, Vladimir Vize, Nikolay Zubov and Nikolay Yevgenov. None is a DLNG vessel, so the off-hire angle does not reach the MLP (https://www.urgewald.org/en/media/danish-shipyard-receives-first-six-russia-linked-arctic-lng-tankers-eu-maritime, 2026-07-02).

Sponsor take-private or unit accumulation - no SC 13D and no SC 13D/A has been filed since 2017 and there has been no Form 4 ever. The only 2026 ownership filing is a passive SCHEDULE 13G by an individual, Thomas W. Herfort, for 1,901,981 units (5.17%), event date 4 August 2026, filed 11 August 2026 - real flow at ~38x average daily volume, but it is on EDGAR and was written up by aggregators, so I treat it as thinly priced rather than unpriced and give it no weight (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000119983526000285/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml).

Refinancing - the four sale-and-leaseback facilities with China Development Bank Financial Leasing (Clean Energy $38.6m, Ob River $51.2m, Amur River $52.7m ~3 years each, Arctic Aurora $125.2m ~9 years, $266.2m total) amortise rather than balloon, $11.0m repaid in Q1 2026, so there is no maturity wall for a refinancing announcement to clear.

The company's own website (dynagaspartners.com, including the /upload_press/ PDF path and the Presentations page) returned HTTP 503 on every attempt on 2026-09-07, and the Wayback API has no snapshot of the presentations page, so I could not front-run the slide deck or diff the fleet table on the company's own pages.

Yamal-side operational distress that would reach DLNG's P&L - Bellona's AIS-derived monthly Arctic report for May 2026 counts 25 Sabetta cargoes to Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Spain and names no Dynagas vessel; and because both Yamal ships are on time charter to 2033/2034, the fact that Yenisei River was drifting at 1.9 knots off southwest Ireland and Lena River was steaming 'FOR ORDERS' on 6-7 September 2026 costs the partnership no hire (https://etc.bellona.org/2026/07/09/monthly-highlights-from-the-russian-arctic-may-2026/, https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9629598).

A quantifiable Q2 revenue surprise - the arithmetic is already public and roughly offsetting: Q1 2026 carried off-hire from unscheduled repairs on two vessels (95.1% utilisation vs 98.8% in Q4 2025) which should not repeat, against roughly three weeks of Clean Energy redelivery gap in April 2026 inside Q2. Q1 revenue was $39.9m and adjusted EBITDA $24.3m; I have no basis to call Q2 materially away from that.
baseline_tension: There is no tension to resolve because the baseline states no priced direction - no EPS estimate, no usable chain, no skew, and a reaction history the sweep correctly flagged as 6-K noise rather than earnings - so the only priced statements available are the tape's: my findings cut hard against the +16% two-session re-rating on 22-23 July, and agree with the -4.94% five-day and -6.2%-from-6-August fade, which is why I size the net well inside the 2.2% median absolute reaction I measured off DLNG's four real prints.
